{
  "project_id": "P-GTM-SmartPublicFinances",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Fragmented and obsolete PFM information systems may cause data inconsistencies and manual processing errors.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop a comprehensive integration plan, adopt an enterprise architecture, and execute phased migration with data reconciliation checks.",
      "evidence": "Core PFM information systems suffer from fragmentation, obsolescence, and weak institutional support."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Cyber‑attacks could disrupt critical public finance systems and compromise sensitive data.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Implement an ISMS (ISO 27000), establish a CSIRT/SOC, conduct regular penetration testing and staff security training.",
      "evidence": "Superintendency of Tax Administration faced >8,000 attacks in 2021; Guatecompras and SICOIN stopped working due to a cyber‑attack in Nov 2023."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Limited analytical capacity restricts use of diagnostic and predictive analytics for decision‑making.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Create a dedicated data analytics unit, provide structured career paths, and deliver intensive training on advanced analytics techniques.",
      "evidence": "96 % of countries rely on descriptive analytics; use of diagnostic and predictive analytics remains minimal."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Fiscal vulnerability due to heavy reliance on remittances and VAT could reduce government revenue.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Build fiscal buffers, diversify revenue sources, monitor remittance trends, and adjust budget assumptions proactively.",
      "evidence": "Remittances amount to 19.4 % of GDP; a decline could reduce VAT collections, which generate 49 % of net income."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Delay in establishing the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) may postpone fund disbursement.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set a clear timeline, treat PIU establishment as a condition of effectiveness, and provide technical assistance to meet the deadline.",
      "evidence": "No withdrawal shall be made under Category 1 until the Borrower has established the PIU, satisfactory to the Bank."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Insufficient political commitment could stall reform implementation.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Secure high‑level endorsement from the Minister of Finance, embed reform milestones in ministerial performance contracts, and maintain a stakeholder coalition.",
      "evidence": "A common reason for failure is lack of adequate preparation and institutional stability; strong, sustained commitment from senior government leadership is crucial."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Low uptake of gender‑responsive budgeting limits inclusive outcomes.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Mandate gender tagging for all municipalities, provide technical assistance, and link compliance to performance incentives.",
      "evidence": "Only 0.6 % of the national budget was tagged with a gender focus; 112 of 340 municipalities linked their budget to the CPEG."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Extreme weather events could damage ICT infrastructure and interrupt system operations.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Design ICT infrastructure to meet resilience standards, locate critical servers in safe zones, and develop climate‑aware business continuity plans.",
      "evidence": "Extreme weather events pose an additional risk that can cause significant infrastructure damage and economic losses."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Procurement of energy‑efficient ICT hardware may experience delays, affecting project schedule.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Engage market early, pre‑qualify suppliers, embed life‑cycle cost criteria, and monitor procurement milestones closely.",
      "evidence": "Implementing ICT equipment will be energy‑efficient and electronic waste treated adequately."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Absence of a data‑governance framework could lead to poor data quality and limited interoperability.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop and adopt a data‑governance model, define standards, assign data stewards, and conduct regular data‑quality audits.",
      "evidence": "Data availability in the repository is limited due to interoperability issues and the absence of a data‑sharing framework."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "High staff turnover may erode newly built analytical and technical capacity.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Institutionalize training, create clear career ladders for data analysts, and implement retention incentives and knowledge‑transfer mechanisms.",
      "evidence": "Lack of structured career paths for data professionals, insufficient training opportunities, and inadequate resourcing."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Coordination gaps among MINFIN, SEGEPLAN and other agencies could cause implementation bottlenecks.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Formalize terms of reference for the Digital Transformation and Interinstitutional Committees, schedule regular joint meetings, and use shared project‑management tools.",
      "evidence": "Digital Transformation Committee and Interinstitutional Committee will serve as governance bodies ensuring inclusive participation."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Delayed or partial adoption of IPSAS may hinder financial reporting improvements.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Set a phased IPSAS adoption timeline, provide IMF‑led technical assistance, and monitor quarterly progress reports.",
      "evidence": "Subcomponent 1.1 includes adopting International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) to improve the quality of financial reporting."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Weak monitoring and evaluation could fail to detect implementation problems early.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen the M&E unit, conduct semi‑annual independent reviews, and deploy real‑time dashboards for key performance indicators.",
      "evidence": "PIU will establish a project monitoring system... semiannual progress reports to the Bank."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Public investment management weaknesses may cause cost overruns and project discontinuities.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Introduce spending reviews, strengthen ex‑ante evaluation criteria, and enforce competitive procurement processes for investment projects.",
      "evidence": "Significant weaknesses impact the effectiveness of investment management, including inadequate prioritization, frequent project discontinuities, weak procurement competitiveness."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Inadequate change‑management could generate resistance to new PFM processes.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop a comprehensive change‑management strategy, run stakeholder workshops, and monitor adoption metrics throughout rollout.",
      "evidence": "Subcomponent 3.1 supports PFM governance and change management to improve coordination and execution."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Dependence on external World Bank technical assistance may limit sustainability if support wanes.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Build in‑house expertise early, document processes thoroughly, and plan a phased hand‑over of responsibilities.",
      "evidence": "The World Bank will provide TA; project relies on TA for system design and capacity building."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R18",
      "description": "Procurement fraud or corruption could inflate costs and undermine project credibility.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply World Bank procurement regulations, enforce anti‑fraud guidelines, and conduct annual independent audits of procurement activities.",
      "evidence": "Procurement will follow World Bank Procurement Regulations and Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Fragmented and obsolete PFM information systems may cause data inconsistencies and manual processing errors.
risks.mitigation: Develop a comprehensive integration plan, adopt an enterprise architecture, and execute phased migration with data reconciliation checks.
risks.evidence: Core PFM information systems suffer from fragmentation, obsolescence, and weak institutional support.

risks.description: Cyber‑attacks could disrupt critical public finance systems and compromise sensitive data.
risks.mitigation: Implement an ISMS (ISO 27000), establish a CSIRT/SOC, conduct regular penetration testing and staff security training.
risks.evidence: Superintendency of Tax Administration faced >8,000 attacks in 2021; Guatecompras and SICOIN stopped working due to a cyber‑attack in Nov 2023.

risks.description: Limited analytical capacity restricts use of diagnostic and predictive analytics for decision‑making.
risks.mitigation: Create a dedicated data analytics unit, provide structured career paths, and deliver intensive training on advanced analytics techniques.
risks.evidence: 96 % of countries rely on descriptive analytics; use of diagnostic and predictive analytics remains minimal.

risks.description: Fiscal vulnerability due to heavy reliance on remittances and VAT could reduce government revenue.
risks.mitigation: Build fiscal buffers, diversify revenue sources, monitor remittance trends, and adjust budget assumptions proactively.
risks.evidence: Remittances amount to 19.4 % of GDP; a decline could reduce VAT collections, which generate 49 % of net income.

risks.description: Delay in establishing the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) may postpone fund disbursement.
risks.mitigation: Set a clear timeline, treat PIU establishment as a condition of effectiveness, and provide technical assistance to meet the deadline.
risks.evidence: No withdrawal shall be made under Category 1 until the Borrower has established the PIU, satisfactory to the Bank.

risks.description: Insufficient political commitment could stall reform implementation.
risks.mitigation: Secure high‑level endorsement from the Minister of Finance, embed reform milestones in ministerial performance contracts, and maintain a stakeholder coalition.
risks.evidence: A common reason for failure is lack of adequate preparation and institutional stability; strong, sustained commitment from senior government leadership is crucial.

risks.description: Low uptake of gender‑responsive budgeting limits inclusive outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Mandate gender tagging for all municipalities, provide technical assistance, and link compliance to performance incentives.
risks.evidence: Only 0.6 % of the national budget was tagged with a gender focus; 112 of 340 municipalities linked their budget to the CPEG.

risks.description: Extreme weather events could damage ICT infrastructure and interrupt system operations.
risks.mitigation: Design ICT infrastructure to meet resilience standards, locate critical servers in safe zones, and develop climate‑aware business continuity plans.
risks.evidence: Extreme weather events pose an additional risk that can cause significant infrastructure damage and economic losses.

risks.description: Procurement of energy‑efficient ICT hardware may experience delays, affecting project schedule.
risks.mitigation: Engage market early, pre‑qualify suppliers, embed life‑cycle cost criteria, and monitor procurement milestones closely.
risks.evidence: Implementing ICT equipment will be energy‑efficient and electronic waste treated adequately.

risks.description: Absence of a data‑governance framework could lead to poor data quality and limited interoperability.
risks.mitigation: Develop and adopt a data‑governance model, define standards, assign data stewards, and conduct regular data‑quality audits.
risks.evidence: Data availability in the repository is limited due to interoperability issues and the absence of a data‑sharing framework.

risks.description: High staff turnover may erode newly built analytical and technical capacity.
risks.mitigation: Institutionalize training, create clear career ladders for data analysts, and implement retention incentives and knowledge‑transfer mechanisms.
risks.evidence: Lack of structured career paths for data professionals, insufficient training opportunities, and inadequate resourcing.

risks.description: Coordination gaps among MINFIN, SEGEPLAN and other agencies could cause implementation bottlenecks.
risks.mitigation: Formalize terms of reference for the Digital Transformation and Interinstitutional Committees, schedule regular joint meetings, and use shared project‑management tools.
risks.evidence: Digital Transformation Committee and Interinstitutional Committee will serve as governance bodies ensuring inclusive participation.

risks.description: Delayed or partial adoption of IPSAS may hinder financial reporting improvements.
risks.mitigation: Set a phased IPSAS adoption timeline, provide IMF‑led technical assistance, and monitor quarterly progress reports.
risks.evidence: Subcomponent 1.1 includes adopting International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) to improve the quality of financial reporting.

risks.description: Weak monitoring and evaluation could fail to detect implementation problems early.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen the M&E unit, conduct semi‑annual independent reviews, and deploy real‑time dashboards for key performance indicators.
risks.evidence: PIU will establish a project monitoring system... semiannual progress reports to the Bank.

risks.description: Public investment management weaknesses may cause cost overruns and project discontinuities.
risks.mitigation: Introduce spending reviews, strengthen ex‑ante evaluation criteria, and enforce competitive procurement processes for investment projects.
risks.evidence: Significant weaknesses impact the effectiveness of investment management, including inadequate prioritization, frequent project discontinuities, weak procurement competitiveness.

risks.description: Inadequate change‑management could generate resistance to new PFM processes.
risks.mitigation: Develop a comprehensive change‑management strategy, run stakeholder workshops, and monitor adoption metrics throughout rollout.
risks.evidence: Subcomponent 3.1 supports PFM governance and change management to improve coordination and execution.

risks.description: Dependence on external World Bank technical assistance may limit sustainability if support wanes.
risks.mitigation: Build in‑house expertise early, document processes thoroughly, and plan a phased hand‑over of responsibilities.
risks.evidence: The World Bank will provide TA; project relies on TA for system design and capacity building.

risks.description: Procurement fraud or corruption could inflate costs and undermine project credibility.
risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank procurement regulations, enforce anti‑fraud guidelines, and conduct annual independent audits of procurement activities.
risks.evidence: Procurement will follow World Bank Procurement Regulations and Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption.
